facts.text: Dutch colonists established a trading post on Manhattan Island in 1624, naming the settlement New Amsterdam in 1626.
The nickname Big Apple dates back to the 1920s, when a reporter used the term to describe horse racetracks.
Manhattan was historically part of the Lenapehoking territory inhabited by the Munsee, Lenape, and Wappinger tribes.
Rucker Park in Harlem is a playground court famed for its streetball style, where many NBA athletes have played.
The George Washington Bridge connects Upper Manhattan to New Jersey and is the world's busiest motor vehicle bridge.
The loss of Penn Station led to a 1965 law establishing the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission.
